title: A fixed cohomology degree of derived tensor depends on finite truncation windows
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and use the abelian category of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and its derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived tensor is the bifunctor computed by total tensors of K-flat resolutions with flat terms [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $K,L\in D(R)$ and $b_K,b_L\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $H^q(K)=0$ for $q>b_K$ and $H^q(L)=0$ for $q>b_L$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For every $i\in\mathbf Z$ and integers $a,c$ with $a\leq i-b_L$ and $c\leq i-b_K$, the canonical good-truncation maps [def-kun-truncations] induce an isomorphism of $R$-module sheaves $$H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i((\tau_{\geq a}K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(\tau_{\geq c}L)).$$ The truncated factors have cohomology only in $[a,b_K]$ and $[c,b_L]$, respectively, with the interval interpreted as empty if its lower endpoint exceeds its upper endpoint. No Noetherian, local-constancy, finite-generation, or existence-of-points hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 094H (lemma-locally-constant-tensor-product), first equality of the proof, with cutoffs corrected to account for the other factor's upper bound; the source's uniform i-1 cutoff is false for shifted complexes (see report.md)

proof.text: Choose complexes representing $K,L$. Put $A=\tau_{\leq a-1}K$, $B=\tau_{\leq c-1}L$, $K^+=\tau_{\geq a}K$, and $L^+=\tau_{\geq c}L$. By the explicit good-truncation cohomology in [def-kun-truncations], $A$ has zero cohomology above $a-1$, $B$ above $c-1$, and $K^+$ above $b_K$. The latter assertion includes $a>b_K$, when $K^+$ is acyclic. The same definition shows that $K^+$ has cohomology only in $[a,b_K]$ and $L^+$ only in $[c,b_L]$. If a lower endpoint exceeds its upper endpoint, all cohomology vanishes. These constructions and their canonical maps are interpreted in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0118 (section-truncations), canonical cochain truncations and their cohomology

proof.text: Use good upper truncation [def-kun-truncations] to represent $A,L,K^+,B$ by complexes with terms zero above $a-1,b_L,b_K,c-1$, respectively. Indeed the upper-truncation inclusion retains all possibly nonzero cohomology and is a quasi-isomorphism, hence invertible in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] to each of these four complexes, preserving its indicated upper term bound. Write the resulting flat complexes as $P_A,P_L,P_+,P_B$. They are K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], the complexes $\operatorname{Tot}(P_A\otimes_RP_L)$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(P_+\otimes_RP_B)$ represent $A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ and $K^+\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B$, respectively. This construction uses only a small ringed site, without points or finiteness conditions.

source.place: Tags 077J (lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero), 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), and 06YU (definition-derived-tor); bounded-above replacements as in the cited replacement node

proof.text: The degree $n$ term of the first total tensor is $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P_A^p\otimes_RP_L^q$ by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. A nonzero summand requires $p\leq a-1$ and $q\leq b_L$, so the entire term is zero for $n>a-1+b_L$. Since $a\leq i-b_L$, this implies vanishing in every degree $n\geq i$, and in particular in degrees $i$ and $i+1$. For the second total tensor, a nonzero summand requires $p\leq b_K$ and $q\leq c-1$, so its term is zero for $n>b_K+c-1$. The inequality $c\leq i-b_K$ again makes all terms in degrees $n\geq i$ zero. Consequently $H^i$ and $H^{i+1}$ of both $A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ and $K^+\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B$ vanish: cohomology in a degree with zero term is zero, by the kernel/image formula of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. No flatness of good lower truncations is claimed.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), with the total-complex formula of homology.tex Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] to $K$ with $b=a$ to obtain $A\to K\to K^+\to A[1]$, with the canonical map $K\to K^+$. Derived tensor is exact in each variable by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], applied to the identity morphism of the ringed topos of $(\mathcal C,R)$; only its sentence asserting separate exactness is used. Tensor this triangle with $L$. The long exact sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] contains
$$0=H^i(A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\longrightarrow H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\longrightarrow H^i(K^+\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\longrightarrow H^{i+1}(A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)=0.$$
The zero terms were proved in Step 3. Exactness makes the middle arrow both monic and epic, hence an isomorphism in the abelian category of module sheaves. The arrow is induced by the canonical truncation map, since it is the second arrow of the tensored triangle.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), Tags 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological) and 0147 (definition-homological); tensor exactness is sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] to $L$ with $b=c$, obtaining $B\to L\to L^+\to B[1]$. Tensor on the left with $K^+$, using separate exactness from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] for the same identity ringed-topos morphism. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] now gives
$$0=H^i(K^+\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\longrightarrow H^i(K^+\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\longrightarrow H^i(K^+\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L^+)\longrightarrow H^{i+1}(K^+\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)=0,$$
again by Step 3, so its middle arrow is an isomorphism. Compose it with the isomorphism of Step 4. Bifunctoriality in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies the composite with $H^i$ of the tensor of the two canonical truncation maps: applying the first map and then the second equals their bifunctor image. This is the asserted canonical isomorphism; the window assertions were proved in Step 1.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q111-248a179da (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all five steps in full, together with the statement of every cited node; there are no new nodes and no files were changed. Source: Stacks 094H (sites-cohomology.tex 14356-14376). Its uniform cutoff tau_{>=i-1} is false: on the one-point site over a field k, K=k[2], L=k[-2], i=0 gives H^0 of the tensor equal to k, but tau_{>=-1}K=0. The item's corrected cutoffs a<=i-b_L and c<=i-b_K are correct and not weakened, and the only citer (lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-tensor) uses exactly these. Step 1: the good-truncation windows follow from def-kun-truncations. Step 2: lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement keeps the term bound N, lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site gives K-flatness, and the descent node gives the Tot model; the hypotheses (same small site, same commutative R) hold. Step 3: the degree count is correct; the Tot terms vanish for n>a-1+b_L and for n>b_K+c-1, both at most i-1, so H^i and H^{i+1} of both tails are zero. Steps 4-5: the truncation triangle (Mathlib leaf, matches derived.tex 08J5), the 'exact in each variable' sentence of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact (its proof uses the descent node, so it is the same bifunctor) and the long exact sequence leaf give two isomorphisms, and bifunctoriality makes their composite H^i(q_K tensor q_L). proof_deps equals the union of uses, and the graph stays acyclic (the item is not in the 484-node dependency closure of its citations). Route: the descent and mate-exact nodes are in the same unit and both lem-sf nodes are Mathlib leaves. The two declared tool uses (lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement, lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site) are accepted as generic black boxes. lean.statement: theorem isIso_derivedTensor_truncationWindow {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w, max u v, (max u v) + 1} (SheafOfModules.{max u v, v, u, max u v} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R))] (K L : DerivedCategory.{w, max u v, (max u v) + 1} (SheafOfModules.{max u v, v, u, max u v} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R))) (bK bL : ℤ) (hK : ∀ q : ℤ, bK < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K)) (hL : ∀ q : ℤ, bL < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj L)) (i a c : ℤ) (ha : a ≤ i - bL) (hc : c ≤ i - bK) : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).map ((wfSiteDerivedTensor J R).map (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ a).app K) ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ c).app L)))) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ bK < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE a).obj K))) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, q < c ∨ bL < q → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE c).obj L)))
